key_insight: An all-atom RF aerogel skeleton model reproduces experimental skeletal density and supports simulation of iron incorporation.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a starting point for screening fillers and dopants for RF aerogels, including potential thermoelectric functionalization.
method: Optimize RF base units with DFT and compare calculated infrared spectra with experiment.
Select COMPASS II by benchmarking branched RF structures against DFT, then equilibrate a 15,012-atom skeleton using MD.
Add 5 wt% iron and track incorporation during 1 ns of NPT simulation.
evidence_signal: Calculated infrared spectra agreed with experiment, simulated skeletal density was 1.296 versus 1.3 g/cm³ experimentally, and embedded iron increased from 63% to 71%.
watch_item: The model aggregates RF units without inter-unit cross-links; agreement with skeletal density does not establish pore-scale structure or long-term dopant stability.
paper_title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
